categories.main_business_segments: Heiwa Real Estate operates two main business segments: the Building Business, which involves the development, leasing, management, and sale of office buildings, commercial facilities, residential properties, and securities exchange buildings; and the Asset Management Business, which includes asset management for Heiwa Real Estate REIT and real estate brokerage services.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: The company leverages expertise in urban redevelopment, property management, and sustainable building operations. It employs advanced property development and management techniques, including energy-efficient building systems, disaster resilience measures, and digital transformation (DX) initiatives to enhance operational efficiency and sustainability.
categories.primary_customers_markets: Key customers include institutional investors, tenants of office and commercial buildings, residential tenants, and real estate investment trusts (notably Heiwa Real Estate REIT). The company primarily serves the financial sector (securities exchanges), corporate tenants, and retail businesses in major urban centers.
categories.geographic_coverage: Operations are concentrated in Japan, with a focus on central Tokyo (notably Nihonbashi Kabutocho and Kayabacho), Osaka, Nagoya, Sapporo, Fukuoka, and other major Japanese cities. There are no significant overseas operations.
categories.supply_chain_position: Heiwa Real Estate operates downstream in the real estate value chain, directly managing, leasing, and selling developed properties to end-users and investors, while also providing asset management services.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: Strategic priorities include expanding redevelopment projects nationwide, enhancing both profit growth and capital efficiency, and advancing sustainability initiatives such as GHG emissions reduction and resilient urban development. The company is also focusing on digital transformation, human capital development, and strengthening alliances with major partners like Taisei Corporation and Mitsubishi Estate.
categories.revenue_model: Revenue is primarily generated from property leasing (offices, commercial, residential), property sales, and asset management fees. Additional income streams include brokerage commissions and hotel operations.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: Major competitors include large Japanese real estate developers such as Mitsubishi Estate, Mitsui Fudosan, Sumitomo Realty & Development, and Tokyo Tatemono. Heiwa Real Estate differentiates itself through its focus on securities exchange-related properties and urban redevelopment, maintaining a strong presence in niche markets like Kabutocho.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: For the fiscal year ending March 2025, consolidated revenue was ¥42.1 billion, with operating profit of ¥13.2 billion and net profit attributable to shareholders of ¥9.6 billion. The company has a stable growth profile, with a focus on capital efficiency (targeting ROE above 7%) and a moderate leverage ratio (net D/E around 1.9x).
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: Heiwa Real Estate emphasizes its ability to create attractive, sustainable urban spaces that enhance community value and future prosperity. Its unique positioning in securities exchange districts, expertise in redevelopment, and commitment to sustainability and stakeholder engagement set it apart from generalist real estate firms.
